# Security interoperability fixtures

These PDFs exercise the Standard security handler across RC4-40 (R2), RC4-128
(R3), AES-128 (R4), and AES-256 (R5 and R6). They are generated by qpdf, so the
tests validate interoperability with an independent, mature implementation
rather than PDFs encrypted by `core-pdf` itself.

The committed files are the test inputs. qpdf is needed only to regenerate them
and is intentionally not a project or test dependency:

```sh
uv run python scripts/generate_security_interop_fixtures.py
```

`manifest.json` records the generating qpdf version, exact commands, test
passwords, expected content, and SHA-256 hashes. qpdf uses fresh random data
while encrypting, so regeneration may update the hashes while preserving fixture
behavior.

The RC4 commands include `--allow-weak-crypto` because qpdf otherwise refuses
to create those obsolete formats. R5 is also generated only to test historical
compatibility. These fixtures are read-only test inputs, not recommended PDF
creation settings.
